purpose: Replace a repeated roadmap paragraph with a concise primary-source comparison of recent magnetic-robot shape and navigation control; preserve the manuscript contribution scope.

background_patch.old: This formulation fixes what information must pass between the four steps. The identification input is a set of observed states with a declared mechanical normalization and error budget. The fitted object is an energy function, so a control decision can use derivatives evaluated away from the observed trajectories. The stability output must then specify a state set and a physical amplitude, rather than only a reconstruction error. Finally, the actuation output must include commands and bounds for the full body. These requirements determine the quantities measured in the experiments: held-out state and tip errors for prediction, step-refinement errors for integration, analytic and nondegeneracy bounds for persistence, and centreline and magnetic-command envelopes for operation. These quantities connect learning accuracy to an admissible motion or command, following the four steps in Table~\ref{tab:core-roadmap}.
background_patch.new: Recent magnetic-robot control studies address shape regulation and lumen navigation directly. \citet{francescon2025shape} combine a pseudo-rigid-link model with vision feedback and homogeneous fields to control a robot with a prescribed lengthwise magnetization profile, demonstrating navigation in a soft pancreatic-duct phantom under varied insertion poses. \citet{tong2025navigation} use a geometrically nonlinear magnetic-rod simulation with reduced contact handling to compute fields that reduce distal-tip constraint forces, with planar phantom experiments and three-dimensional numerical demonstrations. These studies establish practical routes from a mechanical model to magnetic commands. The question pursued here is how a learned energy, with a quantified identification error, can support both persistent motion and bounds on the entire centreline. For the stated planar beam, we connect analytic error and twist bounds to a finite-amplitude invariant torus, realize its low-mode dynamics in the damped full finite-element plant, and bound driven motion through supplied work. Table~\ref{tab:core-roadmap} summarizes the objects passed between these steps.
